newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha stable, eyes on July LSWR allocation.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha stable, eyes on July LSWR allocation.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices were steady on Wednesday, while fuel oil dealers were anxiously awaiting Pertamina's low-sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) allocation for July, traders said.
Allotment for July lifting cargoes was initially expected to be released earlier this week.
"Maybe they (Pertamina) are having a difficult time in figuring out how to divide the limited July cargoes for their affiliates," one trader said.
July allocation was rumoured to be as small as 2.3 million barrels due to a routine closure at the Balikpapan refinery.
Pertamina allocated 3.1 million barrels for June.
Bids for July LSWR cargoes were heard at 80 to 85 cents per barrel over the Pertamina formula against no offers.
"It's not like we are trying to entice higher bids, but we just don't seem to have enough cargoes to sell in the spot market," one fuel oil trader said.
Naphtha trading remained quiet as most regional traders and brokers were still on their way back from an annual naphtha conference held in Tokyo on Monday and Tuesday.
Open-spec naphtha for second-half August was indicated at $198.00/200.00 per tonne in late afternoon trading.
